title: M5 stage35: necessity of a feasible period residue pattern
scope: Original section4 necessity from an actual anchored physical realization; repeated residue entries and vanishing tuple polynomials allowed.

spec.name: M5.ResidueNecessity.anchored_enumeration
spec.statement: ∀ (A : Finset ℕ) (w : ℕ), 0 < w → A.card = w → 0 ∈ A → ∃ u : Fin w → ℕ, Function.Injective u ∧ Finset.univ.image u = A ∧ ∀ i : Fin w, i.val = 0 → u i = 0
spec.guidance:
Use Finset.orderEmbOfFin A hcard as a witness, its injectivity, image_orderEmbOfFin_univ and orderEmbOfFin_zero. Its zero-index value is min A=0 since 0∈A. No sorted-output classification requirement is added: only existence of an anchored enumeration is concluded.
Return tactic lines without leading by. Preserve exact target.

spec.name: M5.ResidueNecessity.reduced_polynomial
spec.statement: ∀ (w T : ℕ) (hT : 0 < T) (u : Fin w → ℕ), Function.Injective u → AdjoinRoot.mk (M5.cyclicModulus T) (M5.SupportPolynomial.ofSupport (Finset.univ.image u)) = AdjoinRoot.mk (M5.cyclicModulus T) (M5.SupportPolynomial.ofResidueTuple (M5.ResidueNecessity.reduceTuple T hT u))
spec.guidance:
Unfold ofSupport and ofResidueTuple. Finset.sum_image with injectivity converts support sum to indexed sum. Map each monomial to its exponent modulo T using quotient_monomial_period T (u i % T) (u i / T) and Nat.mod_add_div. The reduced tuple need not be injective; cancellations and zero polynomials remain allowed.
Return tactic lines without leading by. Preserve exact target.

spec.name: M5.ResidueNecessity.reduced_connectivity
spec.statement: ∀ (w N T : ℕ) (hT : 0 < T) (u v : Fin w → ℕ), T ∣ N → M5.Connectivity.supportGcd N (Finset.univ.image u) (Finset.univ.image v) = 1 → M5.BoundedConstruction.tupleSupportGcd (M5.ResidueNecessity.reduceTuple T hT u) (M5.ResidueNecessity.reduceTuple T hT v) = 1
spec.guidance:
Let d be the residue tuple gcd. It divides T, each u i % T and each v i % T, hence divides u i and v i. Since T|N, d divides supportGcd N by support_gcd_dvd; this gcd is1. Use Nat.eq_one_of_dvd_one. No injectivity or squarefree assumption is needed.

spec.name: M5.ResidueNecessity.signature_restriction
spec.statement: ∀ (a b F : M5.BinaryPolynomial) (N T : ℕ), T ∣ N → F ∣ M5.cyclicModulus T → M5.completeSignature a b N = F → M5.completeSignature a b T = F
spec.guidance:
Use modulus_multiple T N. The gcd at T divides the gcd at N=F. Conversely F divides a,b and M_T. Apply binary_dvd_antisymm and EuclideanDomain gcd divisibility. No irreducibility or squarefree assumption; all multiplicities retained.

spec.name: M5.ResidueNecessity.physical_to_residue
spec.statement: ∀ (N w T : ℕ) (F : M5.BinaryPolynomial) (A B : Finset ℕ), 0 < w → 0 < T → T ∣ N → F ∣ M5.cyclicModulus T → M5.PhysicalOrder.realizes N w F A B → ∃ r s : Fin w → Fin T, M5.BoundedConstruction.anchoredTuple r ∧ M5.BoundedConstruction.anchoredTuple s ∧ M5.BoundedConstruction.tupleSupportGcd r s = 1 ∧ M5.completeSignature (M5.SupportPolynomial.ofResidueTuple r) (M5.SupportPolynomial.ofResidueTuple s) T = F
spec.guidance:
Unpack realizes. Choose anchored enumerations of both supports, reduce their entries modulo T. Apply reduced_connectivity and reduced_polynomial. Apply signature_restriction to physical signatureN, then complete_signature_congruence to the quotient equalities. Anchor is 0%T=0. This constructs the period pattern rather than assuming it.

spec.name: M5.ResidueNecessity.period_necessity
spec.statement: ∀ (N w : ℕ) (F : M5.BinaryPolynomial) (A B : Finset ℕ), 0 < w → F.Monic → F.coeff 0 = 1 → M5.PhysicalOrder.realizes N w F A B → ∃ r s : Fin w → Fin (M5.signaturePeriod F), M5.BoundedConstruction.anchoredTuple r ∧ M5.BoundedConstruction.anchoredTuple s ∧ M5.BoundedConstruction.tupleSupportGcd r s = 1 ∧ M5.completeSignature (M5.SupportPolynomial.ofResidueTuple r) (M5.SupportPolynomial.ofResidueTuple s) (M5.signaturePeriod F) = F
spec.guidance:
Apply period_law F to obtain positive T=signaturePeriodF. F divides M_N because it is the complete signature, so period_law gives T|N. period_law at T and dvd_rfl gives F|M_T. Then apply physical_to_residue. Covers w=1 and F=1; no supplied residue pattern premise.
